reason: This passage (Exodus 3-4) describes God's compassionate response to Hebrew suffering in Egypt. God explicitly states He has 'seen' (רָאֹה רָאִיתִי) the affliction of His people, 'heard' (שָׁמַעְתִּי) their cries, and 'knows' (יָדַעְתִּי) their pains. God attributes their suffering to oppression by Egyptian taskmasters (מִפְּנֵי נֹֽגְשָׂיו), not to the people's own fault. Rather than blaming them, God promises deliverance to a good land. At the passage's conclusion, the people believe precisely because God has 'visited' (פָקַד) them and 'seen' their affliction—there is no leader assigning blame to the suffering people. The text demonstrates God taking responsibility to rescue the oppressed, not condemning them for their affliction.
story: Moses meets Yahweh in the Burning Bush
